node: Secure additive manufacturing equipment and defense-qualified digital manufacturing infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B direct-exposure scan found a compact US-listed universe around secure defense-qualified additive manufacturing: polymer/production printer leaders, metal additive OEMs, certified AM software/MES and quality workflow platforms, and unusually direct aerospace-defense metal AM suppliers. The strongest underfollowed candidates are small-cap AM names rather than traditional defense primes. The key policy-linked hypothesis is that NDAA/CRMN-style qualification and restrictions on China/Russia additive equipment could shift demand toward US/allied printer, materials, software, and inspection ecosystems, but later layers must verify budget authority, contract conversion, balance-sheet runway, and whether defense revenue is material versus marketing language.
